text:
The Elias Pettersson conversation in Vancouver has flipped. Sportsnet writes that he's rediscovering his game in a healthier environment, and the headlines this week are about Manny Malhotra's effect on him. Daily Faceoff went a step further and asked whether it's time to sell high.

That question is fair, because the totals flatter him. He has 18 points in 18 games, 14 of them assists and eight on the power play, but Vancouver has scored 6.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of luck fades. At 5v5 the Canucks get only 44.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he plays, while winning one of their last ten with him in the lineup. The defense of him is that they're about six points worse without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him dragging weak linemates against top competition last season. He's playing over 20 minutes and has 39 hits, which is a center doing the hard parts. The shooting is the quiet bit: four goals on 24 shots. Expect the points to cool even if the game stays good.
headline: Pettersson is back, but the points will cool
